# NotaTV - Raspberry Pi 4 and Pi 5 (64-bit, one image for both)
# The Pi 5 has its bootloader in EEPROM and ignores start_file/fixup_file; it picks bcm2712*.dtb itself.
kernel=Image
arm_64bit=1

# KMS-grafik med nok CMA-hukommelse til hardware-videodekodning
# (the firmware maps vc4-kms-v3d to vc4-kms-v3d-pi4/-pi5 via overlays/overlay_map.dtb)
dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d,cma-512
max_framebuffers=2
disable_overscan=1

# HDMI-CEC håndteres af Linux-kernen (TV-fjernbetjening -> /dev/cec0), ikke af firmwaren
hdmi_ignore_cec_init=1

# hurtigere opstart
disable_splash=1
boot_delay=0
initial_turbo=30

# seriel konsol til fejlfinding (Pi 4: GPIO 14/15, Pi 5: the 3-pin debug UART)
enable_uart=1

[pi4]
start_file=start4.elf
fixup_file=fixup4.dat
hdmi_enable_4kp60=1
dtparam=audio=on
# the kernel's last messages survive a crash and restart (pstore, saved by bootcheck in /data/notatv/logs)
dtoverlay=ramoops-pi4

[pi5]
# 4K60 works on both HDMI ports without extra settings
dtoverlay=ramoops

[all]
# the kernel set in use (the NotaTV updater switches it)
include notatv-slot.txt
